disposition.title: Lins triality formulas for prisms and antiprisms
disposition.statement:
Let ${\cal M}$ be a map, and denote the Euler characteristics of ${\cal M}$, $phial({\cal M})$, and $skew({\cal M})$ by $\chi({\cal M})$, $\chi_p({\cal M})$, and $\chi_s({\cal M})$, respectively. **Lins-triality conjecture.** For $Prism_m$, one has $\chi_s(Prism_m)=\gcd(m,4)-m$, with $skew(Prism_m)$ oriented exactly when $m$ is even, and

$$
\chi_p(Prism_m)=2+\gcd(m,4)-2m=\chi(Prism_m)+\chi_s(Prism_m)-m,
$$

with $phial({\cal M})$ non-oriented. For $APrism_m$, one has $\chi_s(APrism_m)=1+\gcd(m,3)-2m$ with $skew({\cal M})$ non-oriented, and

$$
\chi_p(APrism_m)=3+\gcd(m,3)-2m=\chi(APrism_m)+\chi_s(APrism_m),
$$

with $skew(APrism_m)$ oriented. The formulas were checked up to $n=100$, but the supplied text does not establish them in general.
disposition.source_name: Michel Deza and Mathieu Dutour, “Zigzag structure of complexes”, arXiv:math/0405279 (2004).

disposition.title: The Fomin–Zelevinsky enumerator relation for antichains
disposition.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be a finite root system of rank $n$. Define

$$
H(x,y)=\sum_{k,\ell}h_{k,\ell}x^k y^\ell,
$$

where $h_{k,\ell}$ counts antichains of cardinality $k$ containing $\ell$ simple roots. Let $F(x,y)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\sum_{\ell=0}^{n}f_{k,\ell}x^k y^\ell$, where $f_{k,\ell}$ counts the simplices of the generalized associahedral complex having exactly $k$ positive-root vertices and $\ell$ negative-simple-root vertices. **Enumerative relation conjecture.** One should have

$$
H(x,y)=(1-x)^n F\left(\frac{x}{1-x},\frac{xy}{1-x}\right).
$$

The relation would connect the two-parameter antichain enumerator with the face enumerator of the generalized associahedron. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
disposition.source_name: Frederic Chapoton, “Sur le nombre de reflexions pleines dans les groupes de Coxeter finis”, arXiv:math/0405371 (2004).

disposition.title: Zigzag structures of simplicial complexes of type {3,4}
disposition.literal_statement: Let ${\cal K}$ be a simplicial complex of type $\{3,4\}$, meaning that every $(d-2)$-face is contained in $3$ or $4$ faces of dimension $d-1$. Let $(P_1,\ldots,P_t)$ be the corresponding partition of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and let $l_i$ denote zigzag lengths. **Type-$\{3,4\}$ zigzag conjecture.** The complex is not $z$-uniform if and only if the part sizes are $(\frac d2,\frac d2)$ or all even, except for the simplex; in every non-$z$-uniform case, $\gcd(l_1,l_2)=\min(l_1,l_2)$ for any two zigzag lengths. In the two specified extreme partitions, the maximum and minimum lengths are respectively $\frac{d(d+2)}2$ and $d+2$, or $3d$ and $\frac{3d}2$. For partition $\{1\},\{2,\ldots,d\}$, the complex is $BPyr(\alpha_{d-1})$. For partition $\{1\},\{2\},\ldots,\{d-2\},\{d-1,d\}$, it has the stated orbit counts, zigzag length $6d$, intersection vectors, and parity-dependent orbit sizes from the source. The supplied text gives no resolution.

disposition.title: Binary matroid conjecture for matroids with cycle systems
disposition.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid admitting a **cycle system**, meaning a cycle-system structure as defined in the source. **Binary matroid conjecture.** Every matroid with a cycle system is binary. The source notes that all known examples admitting cycle systems are regular and relates cycle systems to the underlying circuit space. Whether nonbinary examples exist remains open.

disposition.title: The adjacent-row bigrid perfection conjecture
disposition.literal:
Let a bigrid be an array with entries $\gamma(\epsilon,i,j)$, where the indices are taken wherever the entries are defined, and let a bigrid be **perfect** in the sense defined in the paper. **Adjacent-row bigrid perfection conjecture.** Any bigrid satisfying

$$
\gamma(1,i,j)=\gamma(0,i+1,j)
$$

whenever both sides are defined is perfect. The source notes that this conjecture is straightforward to verify when $m=n=2$, but gives no general resolution.

disposition.title: The disjoint-path comparison conjecture for graded graphs
disposition.literal:
Let $G$ be a graded graph with root $\rho$, levels $V_0,\ldots,V_N$, and IID vertex labels with common distribution $\mu$. For an event $B$ of label sequences, let $P(G;B)$ be the probability that some graded path in $G$ has its label sequence in $B$. Let $M$ be the number of distinct graded paths in $G$, and let $G'$ consist of $M$ paths of length $N$ that are disjoint except at $\rho$. **Disjoint-path comparison conjecture.**

$$
P(G;B)\leq P(G';B).
$$

The comparison is known for graded graphs arising from trees, while the source reports only special cases for general graded graphs, including certain cases with $N=2$.

disposition.title: Shareshian–Wachs conjecture for the matching complex homology representation
disposition.literal:
Let $n=2k$ be even. The complexes ${\mathsf {NPM}}_n$ and the poset ${\mathcal L}_n^{(2)}$ have reduced homology groups carrying actions of $S_n$, where $\varepsilon_n$ denotes the sign character of $S_n$. The poset ${\mathcal L}_n^{(2)}$ consists of trees with $n$ bijectively labelled leaves whose nonleaves have degree congruent to $2$ modulo $2$ but are not of degree $2$, and its order-complex homology is concentrated in dimension $t$. **Shareshian–Wachs conjecture.** There is an isomorphism of $S_n$-modules

$$
\widetilde{H}_{3k-4}({\mathsf {NPM}}_n) \cong_{S_n} \widetilde{H}_t(\Delta {\mathcal L}_n^{(2)}) \otimes \varepsilon_n.
$$

This strengthens the stated Shareshian–Wachs theorem, which identifies the restriction of the left-hand side to $S_{n-1}$ with the corresponding homology representation. The conjecture concerns the full $S_n$-module structure and is unresolved in the supplied source.
